notes.meaning: David places his full trust in the Lord as his safe refuge. When others urge him to fly away like a frightened bird to the hills, he questions their advice. He knows that true safety comes from God rather than running to hide in the mountains.

Frightened voices warn of the severe danger threatening the godly. They describe wicked enemies hiding in the shadows with arrows ready on the bowstring, aiming straight at honest people. To human eyes, the ambush looks deadly and inescapable.

The fearful advisers ask what good people can do when law, order, and justice are torn down. When earthly rulers fail and society falls apart, human efforts seem totally powerless. David records this anxious question to show the despair that comes when people look only at earthly trouble.

David answers his advisers by looking up to God in heaven. Even when earthly courts collapse, the Lord remains on His holy throne, completely unaffected by human evil. His eyes closely examine every person on earth, and nothing escapes His notice.

The Lord tests righteous people through hardships to strengthen their faith and refine their character. In contrast, His soul hates the wicked and those who love cruelty. God watches over His faithful servants even while they endure painful trials.

God will send sudden and overwhelming punishment upon unrepentant sinners. The words recall the fire and sulfur that fell from heaven on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those who live by evil will eventually receive the full cup of God's righteous judgment.

The Lord is completely righteous, and He loves what is just and good. He shows His favor and peace to those whose hearts are clean and true. In the end, faithful people will experience His joyful presence and see His face.
